title: EXECCRITIC: Learn to Test, Test to Improve for Coding Agents

numericClaims.quote: On SWE-bench Verified, test quality determines whether feedback helps: holding the base Repair agent fixed, tests from the base Test agent reduce resolved rate from a no-test baseline of 61.2% to 57.3%, whereas tests from GPT-5.6-sol raise it to 65.3%.

Composing the trained agents reaches 72.6% without stronger-model or Oracle feedback at evaluation—4.3 points above the trained Repair agent’s no-test result and 11.4 points above the original baseline (Sections 5.2.2 and 5.2.3).
We first perform supervised fine-tuning on 5,000 chain-of-thought trajectories generated by DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (DeepSeek-AI, 2026) on SWE-ReBench, followed by 200 GRPO steps on SWE-ReBench.
On SWE-bench Verified, generated Test patches raise the resolved rate from 81.5% to 85.7%, a gain of 4.2 points, while Oracle F2P feedback reaches 89.7%, a gain of 8.2 points.
its median and mean numbers of F2P test cases per instance are 3 and 14.43, compared with 1 and 3.03 for Verified.
As shown in Table 1, SFT raises Qwen3.5-35B from 22.2% to 39.6%, a gain of 17.4 points.
Base-to-Gold success increases from approximately 22% without teacher trajectories to 27% with 1K trajectories, 35% with 3K, and 39% with 5K.
Among the 120 trajectories that entered repair, revision required an average of only 13 additional agent turns.
The agent reaches 66.7% on Rust and 58.3% on C++, but success is lower on C and Java, at 26.1% and 2.4%, respectively.

questions.question: What are the three components of the EXECCRITIC scaffold and their roles?
questions.answer: A Test agent that independently generates repository-native tests (a test patch, an exact execution command, and a JSON behavior contract), a fail-closed harness that qualifies the bundle (validating it and requiring a clean failure on the buggy Base repository) and freezes it, and a Repair agent that revises source code from the test's execution feedback without changing the tests; the official evaluator retains final authority.

questions.question: Which backbone is used for both trained agents, and which model serves as the stronger-model reference?
questions.answer: Qwen-3.5-35B-A3B is the trainable backbone for both the Test and Repair roles; GPT-5.6-sol with medium reasoning effort is the stronger-model reference.

questions.question: How do Qwen-generated versus GPT-5.6-generated tests affect the base Qwen Repair agent on SWE-bench Verified?
questions.answer: From the 61.2% no-test baseline, Qwen-generated (Base-35B) tests reduce the resolved rate by 3.9 points to 57.3%, while GPT-5.6-generated tests raise it by 4.1 points to 65.3%; Oracle F2P feedback raises it by 8.2 points to 69.4%.

questions.question: What is Base-to-Gold success, and how does the Qwen Test agent perform on it after SFT and RL?
questions.answer: Base-to-Gold success Qx(b) = Bx(b)Gx(b) requires a generated test to fail cleanly on the Base repository and pass on the Gold (reference-repaired) repository. The Qwen agent rises from 22.2% (base) to 39.6% after SFT (+17.4 points) and 62.2% after RL (+22.6 points), comparable to Codex-5.3 at 61.0%, vs DeepSeek-V4-Flash at 73.4% and GPT-5.6-sol at 87.8%.

questions.question: What resolved rate does composing the two post-trained agents achieve, and how does it compare to baselines?
questions.answer: 72.6% on SWE-bench Verified—4.3 points above the trained Repair agent's no-test Round-0 result of 68.3% and 11.4 points above the original 61.2% no-test baseline—without stronger-model or Oracle feedback at evaluation; with the trained Repair agent, Oracle feedback reaches 77.6%.

questions.question: How many feedback-guided revision rounds and turns per round are allowed, and what happens if none passes the verifier?
questions.answer: At most five feedback-guided revision rounds (Tmax = 5) of 40 turns each after the Round-0 patch; if the verifier has not passed after the fifth revision, the controller ends the episode and force-submits the latest candidate for official evaluation.

questions.question: What reward does official Round-0 success receive in Repair training, and why is it larger than the post-revision reward?
questions.answer: 1.5 for Round-0 resolution versus 1.0 after revision; the larger Round-0 reward preserves strong direct-repair behavior while the trajectory also learns to benefit from test-guided revision.

questions.question: What do the SWE-bench Pro results show about generated-test feedback, and what explanation is offered?
questions.answer: Generated tests improve Pro by only 0.7 points (61.6% to 62.3%) while Oracle F2P feedback adds 11.8 points (to 73.4%); a coverage-based explanation is that Pro requires broader behavioral coverage—median and mean F2P test cases per instance of 3 and 14.43 versus 1 and 3.03 for Verified—so a bundle focused on one issue behavior may leave other required behaviors uncovered.

questions.question: What did the SFT teacher comparison reveal about chain-of-thought visibility?
questions.answer: GPT-5.6-sol trajectories without CoT versus DeepSeek-V4-Flash trajectories with retained CoT differ by only 4.2 points after SFT (35.4% vs 39.6%), but the gap expands to 26.0 points after RL (36.2% vs 62.2%), suggesting reasoning-visible demonstrations better support on-policy learning—though teacher identity and CoT visibility vary jointly, so causality is not isolated.

questions.question: How does the trained Test agent generalize to non-Python languages?
questions.answer: Base-to-Gold success is 66.7% on Rust and 58.3% on C++, but only 26.1% on C and 2.4% on Java, after Python-only post-training (with 62.2% on SWE-bench Verified Python as the in-language reference).

questions.question: How much revision overhead did feedback-guided repair require in the main results?
questions.answer: Among the 120 trajectories that entered repair, revision required an average of only 13 additional agent turns; test generation is a one-time cost per issue and Test source, with the bundle reused across the three Repair runs.
